articles.title: Capital Maritime Finance advances Athens IPO to fund fleet expansion
articles.summary: Capital Maritime Finance Corp. has opened the public offering for its planned listing on Euronext Athens, seeking fresh capital to support its containership investment programme. articles.body: Capital Maritime Finance Corp. has opened the public offering for its planned listing on Euronext Athens, seeking fresh capital to support its containership investment programme. The company is offering up to 42 million new common shares to qualified and retail investors in Greece. The public offering runs from 13 to 15 October 2026, while all company shares are expected to be admitted to the Main Market of Euronext Athens. The public offering and the listing have not yet been completed. IPO price range and fundraising target Capital Maritime Finance has set a binding offer price range of €7.00 to €7.68 per share. The final offer price will be determined through the electronic book-building process and will be identical for qualified, cornerstone and retail investors. The company aims to raise approximately €250 million, although the offering may generate up to €300 million. Assuming proceeds of €250 million, estimated net proceeds after issuance expenses would amount to approximately €239.3 million. Cornerstone investors have committed €70 million to the offering. At least 30% of the new shares, excluding those allocated to cornerstone investors, will be reserved for retail investors, subject to final demand and allocation. Proceeds to support containership programme Capital Maritime Finance currently owns 13 containerships with an aggregate capacity of 27,891 TEUs. Its fleet is expected to grow to 36 containerships following the delivery of 23 additional vessels through 2028. The company’s investment programme amounts to approximately US$1.8 billion. The public offering proceeds are expected to support the financing of this fleet expansion alongside existing bank financing and operating cash flow. articles.title: DP World launches Constanța terminal electrification project
articles.summary: DP World Constanța has launched a €53.8 million project to electrify operations at its container terminal in Romania’s Port of Constanța. The project aims to reduce emissions by replacing fossil-fuel-powered equipment with electric alternatives and installing shore power infrastructure for vessels. Implementation is...
articles.body: DP World Constanța has launched a €53.8 million project to electrify operations at its container terminal in Romania’s Port of Constanța. The project aims to reduce emissions by replacing fossil-fuel-powered equipment with electric alternatives and installing shore power infrastructure for vessels. Implementation is scheduled for completion by 31 August 2028. The European Union will provide a grant of up to €19.7 million through the Connecting Europe Facility. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development will provide a loan of up to €25 million, while DP World Constanța will contribute the remaining funding. Terminal equipment and shore power upgrades The project will electrify 29 container yard blocks through the installation of a busbar system designed to support future electric rubber-tyred gantry cranes. DP World will also develop a charging hub with 10 charging points and acquire 10 electric terminal tractors. Three substations will be installed, each equipped with three 2,000 kVA transformers, alongside approximately six kilometres of busbar infrastructure. Two onshore power supply systems will also be installed for vessels at berth. The systems, supported by two 5 MVA transformers, will supply electricity generated exclusively from renewable sources. The shore power infrastructure will allow ships to switch off their auxiliary engines while berthed, reducing emissions from port stays. Wider investment reaches €100 million The project forms part of a broader electrification programme at DP World Constanța. A second component involves an additional investment of €46.2 million covering remotely operated electric rubber-tyred gantry cranes, two electric mobile harbour cranes and further electric terminal tractors. articles.body: Kongsberg Maritime has secured a contract to design and equip four new offshore wind support vessels for IWS Fleet AS, a subsidiary of Integrated Wind Solutions (IWS). The vessels will be built by China’s Nantong Rainbow Offshore & Engineering Equipment, with the first delivery expected in 2029. The order will expand IWS Fleet’s Skywalker Class series from six to ten vessels. The new Commissioning Service Operation Vessels (CSOVs) will use Kongsberg Maritime’s UT 5519 DEx design. They will support the commissioning, operation and maintenance of offshore wind farms. New vessels to feature advanced propulsion systems Each vessel will accommodate up to 120 people, allowing technicians to live and work offshore during extended assignments. The ships will feature a double-ended design that allows them to move efficiently between wind turbines. This arrangement is intended to reduce manoeuvring time and support daily offshore operations. Kongsberg Maritime will supply electrical power systems, navigation and bridge equipment, propulsion systems, deck machinery and dynamic positioning technology. Each vessel will also feature four rim-drive azimuth thrusters, with two positioned at each end. The thrusters use permanent magnet motors and are designed to improve energy efficiency while providing precise vessel control. Together with the dynamic positioning system, the propulsion arrangement will help the vessels maintain their position during work near offshore wind turbines. Skywalker Class programme expands The latest contract builds on the first six Skywalker Class vessels delivered since 2023. articles.title: Skandia Gateway Quay reinforcement completed
articles.summary: The reinforcement of the south quay at the container terminal at the Port of Gothenburg has been completed on schedule and within budget following more than two years of extensive work by NCC. The completion marks a significant milestone in the Skandia Gateway project, with blasting and dredging works commencing on...
articles.body: The reinforcement of the south quay at the container terminal at the Port of Gothenburg has been completed on schedule and within budget following more than two years of extensive work by NCC. The completion marks a significant milestone in the Skandia Gateway project, with blasting and dredging works commencing on October 13 as the development enters its next major phase. Since spring 2024, NCC carried out reinforcement works along the westernmost 700 metres of the container terminal’s south quay, a technically complex undertaking essential to enabling the deepening of the area closest to the quay. This will allow larger container vessels with deeper draughts to call at the port from the turn of 2028 to 2029. Boskalis Sweden will now carry out blasting and dredging works covering the first 50 metres of water alongside the westernmost 700 metres of the south quay, removing more than 200,000 cubic metres of soft dredged material and approximately 30,000 cubic metres of rock. The area is being designed to accommodate vessels with a maximum draught of 17.5 metres, with works expected to be completed in March 2027. In parallel, the Swedish Maritime Administration is procuring the more extensive blasting and dredging works in the fairway and turning basin alongside modifications to navigational aids, with a contract planned for early 2027 and works scheduled to begin in August 2027. The shared ambition of the Port of Gothenburg and the Swedish Maritime Administration is for the new fairway and quay to become operational before the end of 2028. articles.title: Arabian Gulf Steel Industries sets verified carbon footprint for Rebar
articles.summary: Arabian Gulf Steel Industries, the UAE’s largest private steelmaker and recycler, has achieved the lowest verified carbon footprint for reinforcing bar, establishing a new benchmark for low-carbon construction materials produced in the UAE. The achievement was announced at Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi...
articles.body: Arabian Gulf Steel Industries, the UAE’s largest private steelmaker and recycler, has achieved the lowest verified carbon footprint for reinforcing bar, establishing a new benchmark for low-carbon construction materials produced in the UAE. The achievement was announced at Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi headquarters in the presence of KEZAD Group CEO Mohamed Al Khadar Al Ahmed, AGSI Founder and CEO Asam Hussain and CARES Chief Operating Officer Ayhan Tugrul. AGSI’s rebar produced in Abu Dhabi carries a verified cradle-to-gate carbon footprint of 139 kg of CO2 equivalent per tonne, well below the typical 600 to 700 kg per tonne for scrap-based rebar and below the nearest comparable publicly available Environmental Product Declaration figure of 300 kg CO2e per tonne. Its Sharjah operations record 218 kg CO2e per tonne, also below that benchmark. Both results have been independently verified against recognised international standards, cover production from raw materials to the factory gate and are available as full EPDs on the CARES website. AGSI uses 100% locally recycled scrap and a fully electrified production process, building on its 2024 carbon-neutral plant milestone under PAS 2060. Asam Hussain described the achievement as a defining milestone demonstrating that low-carbon steel production is measurable, verified and being delivered today rather than remaining a future ambition. Abdullah Al Hameli, CEO of Economic Cities and Free Zones at AD Ports Group, highlighted AGSI’s result as establishing the company as a world leader in steel decarbonisation and adding to Abu Dhabi’s standing as a global hub for advanced industry, crediting KEZAD’s infrastructure, utilities and logistics access as enabling manufacturers to achieve internationally competitive performance. articles.summary: Lufthansa Cargo has announced changes to its winter 2026/2027 flight schedule, expanding freighter connections across Asia-Pacific and North America while relocating its Mumbai freighter operations to Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMI). The move to Navi Mumbai took effect on 12 October, transferring freighter...
articles.body: Lufthansa Cargo has announced changes to its winter 2026/2027 flight schedule, expanding freighter connections across Asia-Pacific and North America while relocating its Mumbai freighter operations to Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMI). The move to Navi Mumbai took effect on 12 October, transferring freighter operations from Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (BOM). According to the company, the relocation is linked to infrastructure improvements and plans to increase airport capacity and efficiency. The new winter schedule, which begins on 25 October, will offer 88 freighter routes serving 40 destinations worldwide. Expanded connections across Asia and North America Lufthansa Cargo will offer up to 46 weekly freighter rotations to 17 destinations in the Asia-Pacific region. The expanded network includes Singapore as an additional stop on the existing Frankfurt–Taipei rotation, creating new opportunities for cargo movements within Asia. The carrier will also maintain its increased Trans-Pacific frequency on the Frankfurt–Ho Chi Minh City–Shanghai–Los Angeles route, operating two days per week. In North America, Lufthansa Cargo will increase weekly freighter services to New York JFK to five, Dallas/Fort Worth to four and Houston to three. Its South American network will remain unchanged, with four weekly connections serving four destinations. articles.title: Global Ship Lease secures newbuilding finance
articles.summary: Global Ship Lease has agreed a US$1 billion syndicated loan facility to finance 15 containership newbuildings scheduled for delivery between late 2028 and 2030. The seven-year facility carries an interest rate of SOFR plus 1.5%. Global Ship Lease intends to draw the financing in tranches as each vessel is delivered....
articles.body: Global Ship Lease has agreed a US$1 billion syndicated loan facility to finance 15 containership newbuildings scheduled for delivery between late 2028 and 2030. The seven-year facility carries an interest rate of SOFR plus 1.5%. Global Ship Lease intends to draw the financing in tranches as each vessel is delivered. All 15 ships have secured time-charter employment commencing shortly after delivery. Eight banks support Global Ship Lease loan The oversubscribed facility is backed by an eight-bank syndicate. Bank of America serves as bookrunner, mandated lead arranger, facility agent and security agent. Bank of China (Hong Kong), KfW IPEX and ABN AMRO also act as mandated lead arrangers. CTBC and CaixaBank serve as lead arrangers, while BOCOM Hong Kong and First Citizens Bank participate as arrangers. Tassos Psaropoulos, Chief Financial Officer of Global Ship Lease, said the financing further reduces the risk associated with the company’s newbuilding programme while providing competitive terms and diversified lender support. “The oversubscribed facility involves top-tier banks spanning three continents,” said Psaropoulos. He added that matching each loan tranche with vessel delivery and the commencement of its charter provides greater certainty from both cash-flow and risk-management perspectives. According to the company, the facility’s lending margin is 550 basis points lower than the financing terms available to Global Ship Lease five years ago.
takeaways: Global Ship Lease has agreed a US$1 billion syndicated loan facility to finance 15 containership newbuildings scheduled for delivery between late 2028 and 2030.
The seven-year facility carries an interest rate of SOFR plus 1.5%.
Global Ship Lease intends to draw the financing in tranches as each vessel is delivered.
